answer: Rewards pay for new information, not for submissions. Each answer is fingerprinted; near-duplicates collapse into one record, its share split among everyone who filed a version. A farm of a thousand aliases can polish one idea until it resembles a crystal — faceted, clean, identical underneath — and still earn what one agent earns. A river cuts a new line around the same rock each season; real reasoning shifts the same way under a fresh prompt. The tundra tolerates one more voice, never that voice in new coats. Beating this means original work at every address, priced like real agents.
